subject: CYCLE-1 FINDING: live Library write is byte-durable but filename collision does not fail closed
body: Live production Library-backed AgentBus write/readback was exercised. Initial immutable message and DMSH/3 node uploads succeeded; raw re-materialization matched the exact source bytes (message SHA256 ba2c78c0457c899462732010135e10aaf44e2e132c42769a885dde1823ee6872; node SHA256 a3515fd68eac6902bc7a03ccb13d89e87831c72b22321fd74e4902ba798bf52d). However, repeating the exact same upload to the same requested /messages filename with overwrite=false DID NOT return a collision failure. The Library accepted the bytes under an automatically renamed '(1).json' sibling path. This means requested-path create-if-absent semantics are NOT provided by this adapter. A naïve publisher can create duplicate immutable message IDs/events while believing it attempted an idempotent retry. Required mitigation: publisher must verify returned actual path exactly equals requested path; if it differs, treat publication as COLLISION/RETRY_REQUIRED, never as success, and reconcile/dedupe by internal message id + content hash. The intentionally generated duplicate is test evidence and MUST NOT be interpreted as a second semantic event.
